name: Mini squat
summary: A shallow squat to about a third of the way down, knees tracking over the toes.
setup: Face the phone, feet hip-width, toes slightly out, hands on a chair back if needed. Bend the knees and sit the hips back a little, keeping the heels down, then stand tall.
brief: Feet hip-width, toes slightly out, hands on a chair back if needed. Bend the knees and sit the hips back a little, keeping the heels down, then stand tall.
why: Facing the phone shows both knees at once: the depth from each knee angle, and the classic fault — knees drifting toward each other — as the distance between them shrinking.
progression: Deeper; hold a weight at the chest.
regression: Shallower, or hands on the chair.
contraindications: Pain under the kneecap at the bottom.

faults.label: Knees caving inward
faults.tip: Screw the feet into the floor so the knees track over the second toe. Caving loads the inside of the knee.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.tip: Sit the hips back rather than driving the knees forward; the weight belongs in the whole foot.

faults.label: Weight on the toes
faults.tip: Rocking forward loads the kneecap. Feel the pressure across the whole foot.

faults.label: Going too deep
faults.cue: Small bend — a third of the way
faults.tip: A mini squat is a short range on purpose; depth is added later, once it is painless.

guide.surface: Firm floor, bare feet or flat shoes.
guide.stop: Kneecap pain, or the knee collapsing inward.
guide.cannotSee: How far the hips travel back — that is a side-view detail.

points.t: Track over the toes, staying apart at the bottom.
Only a third of the way down — this is a mini squat.
Heels stay down; weight through the whole foot.
